newsitem.title: USA: Saks in plan to buy Barney's for $290 mln.
newsitem.headline: Saks in plan to buy Barney's for $290 mln.

text.p: Saks Holdings Inc and Isetan Co said late Tuesday they agreed to a joint plan of reorganization for Barney's Inc under which Saks would acquire Barney's stock and assets for about $290 million.
Saks said it and Isetan will submit their joint plan to a New York bankruptcy court for approval.
"We believe the Saks-Isetan joint plan offers a global settlement to, and is the most viable resolution for, all parties in the Barney's bankruptcy," Saks and Isetan said in a joint statement.
Saks said that, under the plan, Barney's unsecured creditors will get about $0.20 for each dollar.
Isetan said that it expects a "significant" loss on its nearly $200 million emergency loan to Barney's.
It did not provide specific figures.
Saks said the investment in Barney's would be accretive to its earnings. It also did not provide figures.
In a separate release, Saks said it expected to earn $0.20 per share in its first quarter, compared with pro forma $0.09 per share.
Barney's, in a separate release, said it has received the Saks-Isetan "term-sheet" and is currently reviewing it.

Sandra Sternberg, a Barney's spokeswoman, said Barney's would not recognize the Saks-Isetan plan as a reorganization plan. She said that, under terms of Barney's bankruptcy protection, the court can only accept a reorganization plan from Barney's itself.
"Saks has submitted a reorganization plan," said Sternberg. "But no one has the right to submit that plan other than Barney's.

Barney's said it plans to move forward with its motion to be heard on Thursday seeking court approval to offer a termination fee and expense reimbursement protections to any investor who submits an approved "investment" proposal regarding Barney's recapitalization.
Barney's also said it will ask the court on Thursday to extend the period in which Barney's has the exclusive right to submit its own reorganization plan.
The company is seeking a 60-day extension, until July 7, to submit the plan. It is also seeking until September 2 to solicit acceptances of the plan, Barney's said.
Neiman Marcus, which has also expressed interest in Barney's, could not be reached to comment.
